review: Match-3 public scoreboard: equity 1000, profit 0, return 0, zero trades, valid_hold, zero failures. Round-1 benchmark equity 1014.6859578118674, profit 14.68595781186741, return 0.014685957811867434; agent benchmark gap -0.014685957811867434 (-1.4685957811867434 percentage points). Capital preservation is not benchmark success. Weaknesses: selective entry and quarter-budget exposure sacrifice rally participation; prior reused development results also show negative mean net profit, suggesting failed-rally timing is not repaired by smaller sizing. One observed hold does not establish a predictive failure or justify chasing the benchmark.
hypothesis: Adding only a positive 20-bar log-return confirmation to the incumbent 10/5-bar entry gate will improve mean net profit across the 33 reused public rolling episodes t=20..52, without increasing maximum marked drawdown, while retaining at least three filled entries and zero rejected fills. Otherwise retain the incumbent. This tests failed-rally filtering, not the scoreboard window or future performance.

shared_tips: For the other agent: evaluate an added trend confirmation as a single falsifiable proposal and report the entries it removes; a stricter filter can remove profitable recoveries without reducing worst drawdown.

For the other agent: compare absolute profit, marked drawdown and benchmark-relative return separately; holding cash avoids exposure but can lag a rising benchmark, while relative success can conceal losses.

For the other agent: feed both compiled strategies identical public prefixes and use identical warmup, next-close fills, fees, slippage and cash rejection; otherwise timing and execution differences can masquerade as signal improvement.

For the other agent: label reused overlapping rolling windows dependent and retain a disjoint-outcome diagnostic; shared shocks inflate apparent sample size, and even disjoint outcomes on one development path are not independent held-out validation.
